```{python}
#| label: setup
#| echo: false
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from pathlib import Path

CSV_PATH = "../pitch_angles.csv"

if not Path(CSV_PATH).exists():
    raise FileNotFoundError(
        f"{CSV_PATH} not found. Run `make get-all-pitch-angles` from the project root and rerun this notebook."
    )

# Read only the columns we need. The file can be large, so we keep the
# footprint small by skipping the image_name column.
df = pd.read_csv(
    CSV_PATH,
    usecols=["dataset_path", "gimbal_pitch_angle", "flight_pitch_angle"],
    low_memory=False,
)
```

```{python}
#| label: tbl-nan-counts
#| tbl-cap: "Missing pitch-angle values per dataset."
#| echo: false
# Count missing angles and total rows per dataset before dropping them
nan_counts = (
    df.groupby("dataset_path", group_keys=False)
    .apply(
        lambda g: pd.Series(
            {
                "total_rows": len(g),
                "rows_missing_angle": g[
                    ["gimbal_pitch_angle", "flight_pitch_angle"]
                ]
                .isna()
                .any(axis=1)
                .sum(),
            }
        )
    )
    .reset_index()
)

# Keep only datasets with at least one missing angle
nan_counts = nan_counts[nan_counts["rows_missing_angle"] > 0]

# Total across all datasets
total_row = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "dataset_path": ["TOTAL"],
        "total_rows": [df.shape[0]],
        "rows_missing_angle": [nan_counts["rows_missing_angle"].sum()],
    }
)
nan_counts = pd.concat([nan_counts, total_row], ignore_index=True)

nan_counts
```

The table above reports, for each `dataset_path` with missing values, the total number of rows and the number of rows that are missing at least one of the two pitch angles.

```{python}
#| label: drop-missing
#| echo: false
# Drop rows with missing angles
df = df.dropna(subset=["gimbal_pitch_angle", "flight_pitch_angle"])

# Common bin edges: 80 bins spanning -90 to 90 degrees
BINS = np.linspace(-90, 90, 80)
```

# Overall pitch-angle histograms

The histogram below shows the distribution of **gimbal** and **flight** pitch angles across all records. Flight angles are drawn on top so the overlap is visible.

```{python}
#| label: fig-overall-histograms
#| fig-cap: "Overall distributions of gimbal and flight pitch angles (-90° to 90°, 80 bins)."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

n_total = len(df)

plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
plt.hist(
    df["gimbal_pitch_angle"],
    bins=BINS,
    weights=np.ones(n_total) * 100 / n_total,
    alpha=0.6,
    edgecolor="black",
    label="Gimbal pitch angle",
)
plt.hist(
    df["flight_pitch_angle"],
    bins=BINS,
    weights=np.ones(n_total) * 100 / n_total,
    alpha=0.6,
    edgecolor="black",
    label="Flight pitch angle",
)
plt.xlim(-90, 90)
plt.xlabel("Pitch angle (degrees)")
plt.ylabel("Percentage (%)")
plt.title("Gimbal vs. Flight Pitch Angle Distribution")
plt.legend(title="Angle type")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Per-dataset histograms

The grid below repeats the same comparison for each unique `dataset_path`.

```{python}
#| label: fig-per-dataset-histograms
#| fig-cap: "Gimbal and flight pitch angle distributions per dataset."
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4

# Unique datasets, sorted for deterministic ordering
datasets = sorted(df["dataset_path"].unique())

ncols = 3
nrows = int(np.ceil(len(datasets) / ncols))

fig, axes = plt.subplots(
    nrows,
    ncols,
    figsize=(ncols * 4, nrows * 3),
    sharex=True,
    sharey=True,
    constrained_layout=True,
)

# Flatten the axes array safely even for a single subplot
axes = np.atleast_1d(axes).ravel()

for ax, dataset in zip(axes, datasets):
    subset = df[df["dataset_path"] == dataset]

    n_subset = len(subset)
    subset_weight = np.ones(n_subset) * 100 / n_subset

    ax.hist(
        subset["gimbal_pitch_angle"],
        bins=BINS,
        weights=subset_weight,
        alpha=0.6,
        edgecolor="black",
        label="Gimbal",
    )
    ax.hist(
        subset["flight_pitch_angle"],
        bins=BINS,
        weights=subset_weight,
        alpha=0.6,
        edgecolor="black",
        label="Flight",
    )
    ax.set_xlim(-90, 90)
    ax.set_xlabel("Pitch angle (degrees)")
    ax.set_ylabel("Percentage (%)")
    # Use the last path component as the title so long paths don't overflow
    ax.set_title(Path(dataset).name, fontsize=10)
    ax.legend(title="Angle type", fontsize=8)

# Hide any unused subplots
for ax in axes[len(datasets):]:
    ax.axis("off")

plt.show()
```
